page: Microsoft Azure E32ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture incorporates a large 260 MB L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory totals 256.0 GB RAM, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 1890 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong capabilities in memory subsystem operations and targeted compute tasks. Large-block uncached memory throughput reaches 208.86 GB/sec read and 90.98 GB/sec write, both placing in the upper quartile. Geekbench scores show top-25% metrics in both single-core (2061.0) and multi-core (17016.0) execution, supported by high throughput in single-threaded gzip compression (31.38 GB/sec) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (199.59 GB/sec). Small model LLM inference text generation (135M) achieves top-tier throughput at 373.84 tokens/sec, while CPU-based inference across larger models (7B and 70B) scales predictably within average tiers.

Resource efficiency is elevated by bundling high-density memory with 1890 GB of local NVMe storage on a dedicated core model, reducing dependence on separate disk provisioning for transient workloads. Tradeoffs include average general-purpose compute metrics in stress-ng multi-core and PassMark database testing relative to compute-focused alternatives. The instance is suited for in-memory databases, large data caches, static web serving infrastructure, and memory-intensive enterprise workloads requiring rapid local temporary storage.
